key_insight: V-Retrver replaces static, language-only Chain-of-Thought reranking with an agentic, evidence-driven loop that actively verifies fine-grained visual cues, reducing speculative reasoning and improving multimodal retrieval accuracy.
problem_solved: Existing multimodal retrieval methods rely on static visual encodings and language-centric CoT, which can produce hallucinations or wrong reranks when visual evidence is ambiguous or requires fine-grained verification.
method: Agentic evidence extraction: the system issues focused visual queries (e.g., region probes or attribute checks) instead of relying solely on frozen global encodings.
Multimodal verifier & iterative reranking: an agentic verifier cross-checks retrieved candidates against extracted visual evidence and iteratively refines rankings.
Evidence-aware CoT: combine explicit visual grounding with reasoning traces so reranking decisions are supported by verifiable image evidence rather than pure language speculation.
impact: Makes multimodal retrieval more reliable and interpretable by grounding reranking decisions in explicit visual evidence, which helps practitioners build safer, higher-precision retrieval systems and diagnose failures more easily.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing image → agentic visual probes → verifier → iterative reranking loop
Before/after example: query with top-k candidates where speculative vs. evidence-backed reranks are highlighted
Heatmap/region overlays illustrating focused visual queries and the evidence used for verification
Bar chart or precision@k plot comparing V-Retrver to language-only CoT baselines
paper_title: V-Retrver: Evidence-Driven Agentic Reasoning for Universal Multimodal Retrieval
paper_authors: Dongyang Chen, Chaoyang Wang, Dezhao SU, Xi Xiao, Zeyu Zhang
